title: KV Cache Health Dashboard — Spec (Fragmentation, Eviction, Compaction, Tail Latency)
author: Allison Grant
body:
## Purpose
This dashboard provides an at-a-glance view of KV cache health for Redwood Serving Runtime across Hosted and Dedicated pools. It is designed to:
- Detect memory fragmentation early (before allocator thrash / OOM risk).
- Attribute tail latency (p95/p99) spikes to allocation/eviction/compaction behavior.
- Support safe canary and staged rollout of KV cache compaction (feature-flagged).
- Provide actionable signals for SRE triage and runtime oncall escalation.

## Intended users
- SRE oncall (Hosted + Dedicated)
- Serving Runtime oncall
- Release engineering during runtime rollouts
- Perf / benchmarking owners during regression reviews

## Data sources + requirements
- Metrics pipeline: runtime -> telemetry agent -> central metrics backend (Prometheus-compatible; queried via Grafana).
- Logs: structured runtime logs for compaction/eviction events (used for drill-down links; not required for base panels).
- Required labels on all KV cache metrics:
  - region (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)
  - pool (e.g., hosted-a100, hosted-h100, ded-<account>-h100)
  - deployment_mode (hosted|dedicated|private)
  - model_family (e.g., llama-3, qwen2, mistral)
  - runtime_build (optional for release comparisons)
  - compaction_enabled (true|false) (derived from runtime config/flag)

## Dashboard variables (Grafana)
1) $deployment_mode: hosted, dedicated, private (default: hosted)
2) $region: multi-select (default: all)
3) $pool: multi-select (default: all)
4) $model_family: multi-select (default: all)
5) $compaction_enabled: all/true/false (default: all)
6) $window: rate/quantile evaluation window (default: 5m)

## Metric naming (canonical)
Note: exact names must match the telemetry schema from ENG-2842 / PR-18423. If names differ, update this page and the dashboard JSON together.

### Fragmentation + capacity
- runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio (gauge, 0.0–1.0)
  - Definition: 1 - (allocated_live_blocks / allocated_total_blocks) adjusted for reserved segments. See runtime architecture page for precise accounting.
- runtime_kv_cache_free_blocks (gauge, blocks)
- runtime_kv_cache_total_blocks (gauge, blocks)
- runtime_kv_cache_reserved_blocks (gauge, blocks)
- runtime_kv_cache_active_sequences (gauge, count)

### Allocator pressure + failures
- runtime_kv_cache_alloc_attempts_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total (counter)
  - Failure includes: allocation failure requiring eviction, and hard failure (request rejected / OOM-prevented admission control).
- runtime_kv_cache_reallocations_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_allocator_search_us (histogram)
  - Time spent searching free lists / block maps per alloc operation.

### Eviction
- runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_evicted_blocks_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_eviction_reason_total{reason=...} (counter)
  - Suggested reasons: ttl, pressure, fairness, prefix_cache_conflict, admission_control

### Compaction
- runtime_kv_cache_compaction_runs_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total (counter)
- runtime_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_time_ms (histogram)
- runtime_kv_cache_compaction_cpu_time_ms (histogram)
- runtime_kv_cache_compaction_budget_exhausted_total (counter)

### Latency (request-level)
- runtime_request_latency_ms{route=..., phase=...} (histogram)
  - Phases should include at minimum: end_to_end, prefill, decode
- runtime_request_timeouts_total (counter)

## Dashboard layout
The dashboard is a single page with sections. Panels should support drill-down by clicking series (pool/region/model_family) to jump to:
- Per-pool detail dashboard (optional)
- Logs explorer filtered by region/pool/runtime_build
- Runbook: Mitigating KV cache fragmentation incidents

### Section A — Summary (top row)
A1) "Tail latency (p95/p99) by pool" (Time series)
- Query: histogram quantiles over runtime_request_latency_ms{phase="end_to_end"}
- Split series: pool
- Notes:
  - Provide toggles for p95 and p99 (two queries / two lines per pool is too noisy; default show p99 only).

A2) "KV cache fragmentation ratio (max by pool)" (Time series)
- Query: max(runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio) by (pool)
- Threshold lines:
  - 0.25 (warning)
  - 0.35 (critical)

A3) "Allocation failures rate" (Stat)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total[$window]))
- Display: failures/sec + sparkline
- Drill-down: link to Section C

A4) "Compaction enabled coverage" (Pie/Bar)
- Query: count by (compaction_enabled) of up{job="serving-runtime"}
- Purpose: validate canary/staged rollout is actually applied.

### Section B — Fragmentation + capacity
B1) "Fragmentation ratio (p50/p90/p99 across instances)" (Time series)
- Query: quantile_over_time / prom histogram alternative not available; use:
  - p50: quantile(0.50, runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio) by (pool)
  - p90: quantile(0.90, runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio) by (pool)
  - p99: quantile(0.99, runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio) by (pool)
- Note: If backend doesn’t support quantile() over gauges reliably, fallback to max/avg.

B2) "Free blocks vs total blocks" (Time series)
- Query: sum(runtime_kv_cache_free_blocks) by (pool) and sum(runtime_kv_cache_total_blocks) by (pool)
- Visualization: stacked area (free + used) or two lines.

B3) "Active sequences" (Time series)
- Query: sum(runtime_kv_cache_active_sequences) by (pool)
- Purpose: correlate fragmentation with concurrency.

B4) "Allocator search time (p99)" (Time series)
- Query: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(runtime_kv_cache_allocator_search_us_bucket[$window])) by (pool)
- Purpose: early signal of allocator thrash.

### Section C — Allocation pressure + failures
C1) "Allocation attempts vs failures" (Time series)
- Attempts: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_attempts_total[$window])) by (pool)
- Failures: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total[$window])) by (pool)
- Add derived series: failure_rate = failures/attempts (Grafana transform recommended).

C2) "Reallocations rate" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_reallocations_total[$window])) by (pool)
- Interpretation: realloc spikes typically precede p99 degradation under burst.

C3) "Top pools by allocation failures" (Table)
- Query: topk(10, sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total[15m])) by (region, pool, model_family))
- Columns: region, pool, model_family, failures/s

### Section D — Eviction behavior
D1) "Evictions rate" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_evictions_total[$window])) by (pool)

D2) "Eviction reasons" (Stacked bar)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_eviction_reason_total[$window])) by (pool, reason)
- Purpose: catch unexpected eviction modes (e.g., fairness-evictions dominating).

D3) "Evicted blocks per second" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_evicted_blocks_total[$window])) by (pool)

### Section E — Compaction cost + effectiveness
E1) "Compaction runs rate" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_runs_total[$window])) by (pool)
- Expected: low/steady; high rates indicate thrash.

E2) "Bytes moved rate" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_bytes_moved_total[$window])) by (pool)

E3) "Compaction GPU time (p95/p99)" (Time series)
- Query:
  - p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_time_ms_bucket[$window])) by (pool)
  - p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_time_ms_bucket[$window])) by (pool)
- Purpose: ensure compaction stays within latency budget.

E4) "Compaction CPU time (p95/p99)" (Time series)
- Same as E3, using runtime_kv_cache_compaction_cpu_time_ms.

E5) "Budget exhausted events" (Stat + time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_budget_exhausted_total[15m])) by (pool)
- Interpretation: Some exhaustion is acceptable under burst; sustained exhaustion suggests budgets too low or fragmentation too high.

E6) "Fragmentation delta around compaction" (Annotation + guidance)
- If event annotations are available from logs/derived metrics, overlay compaction runs on fragmentation ratio.
- If not, include a text panel explaining expected pattern:
  - fragmentation ratio should drop shortly after compaction runs; if it doesn’t, compaction is ineffective or blocked by in-flight constraints.

### Section F — Tail latency correlation (diagnostic)
F1) "p99 latency vs fragmentation ratio (same axis group)" (Time series)
- Query 1: p99 end-to-end latency by pool
- Query 2: fragmentation ratio by pool
- Goal: quick visual correlation.

F2) "Timeouts rate" (Time series)
- Query: sum(rate(runtime_request_timeouts_total[$window])) by (pool)

F3) "Latency by phase (prefill vs decode)" (Time series)
- Query: p99 prefill and p99 decode; split by pool
- Interpretation: fragmentation issues often appear during decode bursts but can surface in prefill under mixed long-context traffic.

## Alerting spec (Grafana alert rules)
Alerts are designed to be actionable and to minimize false positives during expected burst patterns.

### Alert 1 — KV fragmentation critical (per pool)
- Condition: max_over_time(runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio{...}[10m]) > 0.35
- For: 10m
- Labels: severity=page, component=kv-cache
- Routing:
  - Hosted pools: page SRE oncall
  - Dedicated pools: page SRE oncall + notify Dedicated support channel
- Runbook: Mitigating KV cache fragmentation incidents

### Alert 2 — Allocation failures elevated (per pool)
- Condition: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total[5m])) by (pool) > 0.5
- For: 5m
- Severity: page (hosted), ticket (dedicated unless paired with p99 regression)
- Notes:
  - If allocation failures are non-zero but p99 is stable, treat as warning (tune thresholds per pool size).

### Alert 3 — p99 latency regression with fragmentation signal (correlated)
- Condition (two-part):
  1) p99 end_to_end latency increases > 25% vs 7d baseline (Grafana anomaly or recording rule)
  2) fragmentation ratio > 0.25
- For: 15m
- Severity: page
- Purpose: reduce paging on latency-only incidents that are not KV related.

### Alert 4 — Compaction overhead risk (GPU time)
- Condition: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (pool) > 5ms
- For: 10m
- Severity: ticket (default), page if concurrent with p99 regression
- Notes:
  - This threshold should be revisited after initial canaries. The intent is to catch pathological sync/stream contention.

### Alert 5 — Compaction thrash (run frequency)
- Condition: sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_runs_total[10m])) by (pool) > 2
- For: 20m
- Severity: ticket
- Interpretation: frequent compaction is often worse than fragmentation; indicates triggers too aggressive or insufficient free space.

## Recommended default thresholds (for panels)
These are UI thresholds, not necessarily paging thresholds:
- Fragmentation ratio:
  - < 0.20: good
  - 0.20–0.25: monitor
  - 0.25–0.35: degraded
  - > 0.35: critical
- Allocation failure rate (failures/sec):
  - 0: good
  - 0–0.1: monitor
  - 0.1–0.5: degraded
  - > 0.5: critical (pool-dependent)
- Compaction GPU p99:
  - < 2ms: good
  - 2–5ms: monitor
  - > 5ms: investigate

## Drill-down links (required)
Each panel should include links with template variables preserved:
- "Open runbook" -> confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/mitigating-kv-cache-fragmentation-incidents
- "Open scheduler/overload dashboard" -> (existing dashboard) with same region/pool vars
- "Logs: compaction events" -> logs explorer query: region="$region" pool="$pool" (message contains "kv_compaction" OR "kv_evict")

## Ownership + maintenance
- Primary owner: Eng Platform (Dashboards/Alerts)
- Metric definitions owner: Serving Runtime (KV cache)
- Alert routing owner: SRE

Update cadence:
- Any metric rename or label changes must be accompanied by:
  1) PR to dashboard JSON
  2) Update to this page (Spec)
  3) Note in release checklist for compaction rollout

## Acceptance criteria
- Dashboard can answer within 2 minutes:
  - "Is p99 spiking in a specific region/pool?"
  - "Is fragmentation rising, and is it causing allocator failures?"
  - "Are evictions/compaction responsible, and what is the overhead?"
- For a canary pool, dashboard can isolate compaction_enabled=true series and compare against false.
- Alert rules produce no more than 1 false positive page/week per region during normal traffic variability (post-tuning period).

## Appendix: Example PromQL snippets
- Fragmentation max by pool:
  - max(runtime_kv_cache_fragmentation_ratio{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", region=~"$region", pool=~"$pool", model_family=~"$model_family"}) by (pool)

- Allocation failure rate per pool:
  - sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_alloc_failures_total{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", region=~"$region", pool=~"$pool"}[$window])) by (pool)

- p99 end-to-end latency per pool:
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_ms_bucket{phase="end_to_end", deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", region=~"$region", pool=~"$pool"}[$window])) by (le, pool))

- Compaction GPU p99 per pool:
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_kv_cache_compaction_gpu_time_ms_bucket{deployment_mode=~"$deployment_mode", region=~"$region", pool=~"$pool"}[$window])) by (le, pool))
